---
title: "Reporting & trust (legitimacy and cooperation)"
toc: true
---

## What it is
Many crime outcomes depend on whether victims/witnesses:
- report incidents,
- cooperate with investigation.

Legitimacy/trust affects reporting and cooperation, which affects detection and deterrence.

---

## Canonical setup (three-stage)
1) Offender chooses $C$ or $N$.
2) If $C$, victim decides report $R$ or not $\bar R$.
3) If report, police choose effort $e\in\{0,1\}$ (low/high). Detection occurs with probability:
$$
q = q_0 + \alpha e
$$
with $q_0\in(0,1)$, $\alpha>0$, and $q\le 1$.

Victim reporting has cost $c_R>0$.  
Victim benefit from successful detection is $B>0$ (justice, safety).  
Police effort cost is $k>0$.  
Legitimacy/trust parameter $L$ increases perceived benefit (or reduces reporting cost). Use:
$$
B(L)=B_0 + \lambda L,\quad \lambda>0.
$$

---

## Solving the victim decision (threshold)
If crime occurs and victim anticipates police effort choice $e$, expected benefit from reporting:
$$
\text{Benefit} = q \cdot B(L) = (q_0+\alpha e)\,B(L).
$$
Victim reports iff:
$$
(q_0+\alpha e)\,B(L) \ge c_R.
$$

This yields a threshold legitimacy level $L^*$ when $B(L)$ is linear:
$$
(q_0+\alpha e)(B_0+\lambda L)\ge c_R
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
L \ge \frac{c_R}{\lambda(q_0+\alpha e)} - \frac{B_0}{\lambda}.
$$

---

## Interpretation
- Higher legitimacy $L$ increases reporting.
- Higher police effort effectiveness $\alpha$ increases the value of reporting (complements).
- If legitimacy rises, **recorded crime may rise** (more reporting) even if incidence falls.

---

## Linking back to deterrence
If offenders anticipate higher reporting and higher detection, the expected cost of crime rises:
deterrence can strengthen without changing formal sanctions.

---

## Later-on analysis
- Allow police effort $e$ to depend on workload/capacity.
- Add strategic police incentives (recording vs clearance metrics).
- Add offender adaptation (switch to low-reporting offenses).
